correctness.rationale: For each insertion gap, valid lower sets are chainwise prefixes and upper sets chainwise suffixes; a simultaneous nonempty lower and upper set is possible precisely when both occupy the same original chain. This proves \(G(i,j)\). Expanding the walk sum gives identity (1), whose nonnegative terms yield exactly the segregated minima. Completing squares around \(r_j=j+(a-b-1)/2\) and respecting monotone \(q_j\) yields all integer maximizers; evaluating the square sum gives the parity formulas. The included checker enumerated 48,602 shuffle words with \(a,b\le8\), and performed 240 direct ternary-transitivity comparisons for \(a+b\le7\), all consistent, without relying on finite tests for the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The object is a natural finite-base orbit-count statistic in the Fraisse limit of all linearly ordered posets. With identical unexpanded reduct (a disjoint two-chain poset), varying only its linear extension changes the number of complete one-types by a cubic amount in the balanced case. Both sharp extrema and every maximizing/minimizing shuffle are classified for arbitrary chain lengths, with a parity-controlled exponential multiplicity of maximizers and a limiting \(3/2\) range ratio. This supplies structural sensitivity information not present in the ambient classification or single-chain calculations.
